hook: A U.S. Navy O-2 pilot from squadron 482ATKS filed this standardized Range Fouler Debrief Form on August 31, 2020, reporting radar contact with multiple UAP objects at 18,000 feet that demonstrated differential speeds and simultaneous formation behavior.
why_it_matters: This report documents a multi-object UAP encounter captured on radar by an active military pilot, with the second object explicitly described as surpassing the first at 'much higher speed' despite identical size and shape — a performance characteristic with no conventional explanation offered. The document was processed through the SPEAR program, which sanitizes identifying information before analysis, illustrating the institutional pipeline that routes aviator UAP reports for collection. Its release under USCENTCOM MOR 26-0028 places this event in the CENTCOM area of responsibility, consistent with the Arabian Gulf location in the manifest, despite the title referencing Japan.

key_findings.finding: The pilot observed an initial UAP on radar, which was then overtaken by a second object of identical size and shape but traveling at substantially higher speed.

quotes.text: Saw the initial object fly through the screen and started tracking i . Initial object was surpassed by another object of same size and shape but much higher speed.

key_findings.finding: At one point during the engagement, three UAP were simultaneously visible on the radar screen, exhibiting relative motion among each other.

quotes.text: At one p4int during tracking the objects, there were three on the screen at the same time moving amongst each other.

key_findings.finding: The contact was at a constant altitude of 18,000 feet and was moving on a bearing of 150 degrees at 230 knots.

The object's shape did not match any standard category on the form (round, square, balloon, or winged); 'Other Shape' was checked alongside 'Apparent Propulsion,' consistent with the metadata characterizing it as sphere/orb or rectangle/cube with metallic properties.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This standardized Range Fouler Debrief Form filed through the SPEAR program represents the formal military UAP reporting pipeline that feeds the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office and its predecessors.
Radar-based UAP tracking data of this type historically flowed through Air Force technical analysis centers, though no direct Wright-Patterson connection is stated in the document.
